Hon'ble Mrs. Manju Rani Chauhan,J.
Heard Mr. Vatsya Narayan, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Rahul Chaudhary, learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondents.

The writ petition has been filed by the petitioners with a prayer to set-aside the part of the interim order dated 18.08.2023 passed by Appellate Tribunal Moradabad in F.S.S.A. Brief facts of the case are that an inspection was carried out on 15.09.2021 at about 11:40 a.m. by the Food Safety Officer of the shop of petitioner no.3, where petitioner no.1 was the food business operator and petitioner no.2 was the distributor of the Ghee (Paras Brand).

sentences.text: A sample was taken and sent for analysis, wherein as per the analysis report, notice was given to the petitioner to which he submitted a reply.

In the proceedings as initiated against the petitioners by a complaint filed under Section26(2)(ii)/51 of the Food Safety Standards Act, 2006, an order was passed on 20.07.2023 by the Additional District Magistrate (Administration), District-Bijnor without considering the reply of the petitioner as submitted to the notice on the complaint so filed, imposing penalty, individually on the petitioners.

The aforesaid order was challenged by means of filing an appeal, which has been decided by order dated 18.08.2023, wherein the interim application has been allowed to the extent that the petitioners shall deposit 50% of the amount of penalty as imposed within a period of one month.
Hence, this petition has been filed by the petitioners.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that reply of the petitioner has not been considered and without assigning any reason for imposing such a penalty, the initial order was passed and the stay application has been allowed to the extent of directing the petitioners to deposit 50% of the amount imposed as penalty within a period of one month.

He further submits that a surprise inspection was conducted without giving proper notice as required under law within stipulated period and without considering the reply of the petitioner, the initial order was passed and the stay application has not been considered keeping the aforesaid facts in mind.
Thus, the order imposing penalty of 50% is illegal and unjustified.
He further requests that a direction may be issued to the competent authority to decide the appeal, within stipulated period and till then no recovery may be made from him.
Learned
Standing Counsel supports the order impugned.
This Court finds that the case of the petitioner has not been considered in its true spirit, and the reply given by him does not find mention in the impugned order.
There is no reason as to why the 50% of penalty has to be deposited by the petitioner.

Considering the facts and circumstance of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and in the interest of justice, particularly in view of the fact that the order imposing penalty is without reason, this writ petition is finally disposed off with a direction to the Appellate Tribunal Moradabad, to decide the appeal so filed by the petitioner, in accordance with law, after giving opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned, by means of a reasoned and speaking order,
preferably within a period of three months, from the date of production of certified copy of this order, if there is no legal impediment, subject to deposition of Rs.50,000/- by the petitioner before the court below within a period of one month from today.
Till a period of one month from today the order impugned dated 18.08.2023 shall be kept in abeyance.
The court below shall decide the appeal without being influenced by the order passed by this Court.
